title: nixos/h2o: enable HTTP/3 via QUIC
reason: Applicable: real h2o module + wired test (multi-file test target). Real diff adds a genuinely new quic mkOption nested under each per-vhost tls submodule, wired into a real lib.optional (value.tls.quic != null) predicate.
targets_toml: single target h2o (module=vhost-options.nix, the per-vhost submodule file), cfg_ident=cfg, option_prefix=[services,h2o,vhosts,*,tls], watch=[quic]. Two option_prefix depths tried (with and without the trailing tls segment); discovered_options consistently lists the real declaration as a 2-segment relative path ['tls','quic'] regardless of which option_prefix depth was used, suggesting discovered_options may not be reported strictly relative to option_prefix the way I assumed -- did not fully resolve the ambiguity in the time available.

additional_raw_facts_for_reviewer.note: AMBIGUOUS -- quic IS a real, present declaration (confirmed via discovered_options showing ['tls','quic'] under the per-vhost submodule) but my watch targeting could not get it to resolve as found under either of the two option_prefix depths tried. Possibly a genuine wildcard/nested-submodule resolution limitation (a shape somewhat like the wstunnel/S4-batch4 wildcard-attrsOf gap, but one level deeper: wildcard-instance -> nested-submodule -> leaf), possibly my own targeting limitation given ambiguity about how oba's watch/option_prefix interact for doubly-nested paths under a wildcard. Flagging honestly as unresolved rather than asserting either way.
